comparisons.peer_topic: Fair value hedge carrying value mechanics
comparisons.peer_summary: The table summarizes the carrying value of hedged assets and liabilities designated in fair value hedging relationships; open hedges synthetically convert hedged items to variable-rate instruments with no earnings impact, while de-designated hedges result in amortization or accretion of cumulative adjustments into earnings.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the mechanics of cumulative fair value hedging adjustments upon de-designation. Goldman Sachs notes that its cumulative adjustments for de-designated items were not material. Bank of America explains the accounting treatment: while open hedges have no earnings impact, if an open hedge is de-designated, the cumulative fair value adjustments are amortized or accreted into earnings over the remaining life.

sentences.text: In addition, cumulative hedging adjustments for items no longer designated in a hedging relationship were not material as of both December 2024 and December 2023.

If an open hedge is de-designated prior to the derivative's maturity, any cumulative fair value adjustments at the de-designation date are then amortized or accreted into earnings over the remaining life of the hedged assets or liabilities.

comparisons.peer_summary: For portfolio layer method closed portfolios, the amortized cost was $72.8 billion and $83.9 billion, with designated hedged amounts and cumulative basis adjustments of $(1.7) billion and $(165) million at Dec 31, 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan disclose the status of cumulative basis adjustments for de-designated hedging relationships. Goldman Sachs states these adjustments were not material for both 2024 and 2023. In contrast, JPMorgan quantifies significant cumulative basis adjustments of $(1.7) billion and $(165) million for 2024 and 2023, respectively, explicitly breaking down the discontinued (de-designated) portions as $(566) million and $(238) million.

sentences.text: In addition, cumulative hedging adjustments for items no longer designated in a hedging relationship were not material as of both December 2024 and December 2023.

At December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, the cumulative amount of basis adjustments was $(1.7) billion and $(165) million, which is comprised of $(1.2) billion and $73 million for active hedging relationships, and $(566) million and $(238) million for discontinued hedging relationships, respectively.
